answer: Each agent can be represented by a key, but keys are cheap, so an economy should require a scarce stake before an agent can earn trust-weighted rewards. For example, an agent registers a bond and loses part of it when a randomly selected, independently verified task is shown to be fraudulent; honest agents recover the bond. An attacker can still create many identities, but must lock capital in each and risks losing it, making fake identities costly rather than free. An orchard, bridge, or dune can name a task domain, not serve as proof of identity.
